subject: general
question: For a spherical mirror, the distance between the pole and the centre of the curvature is:

options.text: half of the radius of curvature
twice the distance between pole and F
equal to the distance between c and F

solution:
The correct answer is **__Option 2__.****
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Pole (P/O)**: Geometric center of the spherical surface of the mirror.
 
• **Centre of curvature (C)**: Centre of the sphere of which the mirror is a part.
 
• **Focus point**: The point where incident rays parallel to the principal axis meet or seem to be met.

 [IMAGE: https://images.collegedunia.com/public/image/I1_ff9111ab56f7656fcc6e01acf00873db.png] 

 
• For a small spherical mirror, the **principal focus ‘F’** lies exactly at the midpoint of the** pole P** and the** center of curvature C. **
 
• Therefore, the focal length of a spherical mirror (concave or convex) is equal to half of its radius of curvature.
 
• Or, The distance between the pole and the center of the curvature is twice the distance between the pole and the focus.
 
• This means if **R = distance between the center of the curvature and the pole (Radius of curvature), f = distance between the focus point and the center of curvature (focal length).**
 
• Then **R = 2f.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Some other useful terms -**
 
• **Principal Axis -** the straight line passing through the center of curvature C and pole P of a spherical mirror, produced on both sides.
 
• **Aperture -** The portion of a mirror from which the reflection of light actually takes place is called the aperture of the mirror. It is also called the linear aperture of the mirror. The aperture of a spherical mirror is denoted by the diameter of its reflecting surface.
 
• **Types of spherical mirror -**__
 
• ***There are two types of spherical mirrors - ***
 
• **1**. Convex Spherical Mirror: whose inner (cave type) surface is silvered and reflection takes place at the outer (convex) surface.
 
• **2.** Concave Spherical Mirror: whose outer bulged surface is silvered and reflection takes place from the inner hollow (cave type) surface.
